claims.text: In sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, surface energy dominates configurational-entropy stabilization.
The surface-energy contribution relative to bulk free energy scales as 1/r in sub-10 nm particles.
Au and Cu have significantly lower surface energies than Co, Ni, and Pt.
Au and Cu have higher vapor pressures than Co, Ni, and Pt under the proposed heating conditions.
Au and Cu segregate to the nanoparticle surface to lower the total surface energy.
Au/Cu surface segregation creates a chemical-potential gradient that drives rapid atomic diffusion.
Above the critical temperature, the segregation driving force exceeds the activation barrier for diffusion.
The critical temperature for active diffusion, segregation, and evaporation is approximately 400-500 K.
Surface-enriched Au and Cu evaporate and thereby cause nanoparticle mass loss and shrinkage.
Smaller nanoparticles evaporate faster, causing loss of particle number density and widening of the size distribution.
Elliptical nanoparticles become spherical because reducing surface area lowers their surface energy.
Icosahedral nanoparticles reshape and evaporate faster than truncated octahedra because they expose higher-energy facets.
Truncated-octahedral nanoparticles are closer than icosahedral nanoparticles to the Wulff equilibrium shape.
The surface-driven mechanism dominates for particles smaller than 10 nm.
For particles larger than 50 nm, bulk entropy and sluggish diffusion dominate and surface-driven segregation is negligible.
The proposed mechanism applies particularly to alloys whose elements have large contrasts in surface energy and vapor pressure.
PLD-grown AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles initially occupy a metastable FCC state produced by kinetic trapping.
EDS mapping during heating will show Au and Cu enrichment at the surfaces of the remaining particles.
The FCC structure may either persist or transform depending on the composition remaining after evaporation.
High configurational entropy and sluggish atomic motion are proposed in the prevailing model to stabilize FCC HEAs against structural change.

contradictions.description: The mechanism is assigned an onset near 400-500 K and mass loss is predicted above 450 K, whereas the falsification rule uses negligible behavior below 600 K. This makes the operational threshold ambiguous, although absence throughout the entire sub-600 K range would still contradict the prediction.
